geographic_bounds._disclosure: PTF-CINCINNATI-MARKET-FACTORY-001 tri-state regional bounding box, corrected mid-run from an Ohio-only boundary to the full Cincinnati, OH-KY-IN metropolitan market per operator instruction. Covers 5 Ohio counties (Hamilton, Butler, Warren, Clermont, Brown), 7 Kentucky counties (Boone, Kenton, Campbell, Grant, Pendleton, Gallatin, Bracken) and 3 Indiana counties (Dearborn, Franklin, Ohio). Northernmost: Middletown OH / Franklin County IN (padded to 39.60). Southernmost: Bracken County KY (Brooksville, padded to 38.55). Westernmost: Gallatin County KY / Franklin County IN (padded to -85.10). Easternmost: Lebanon / Pendleton County KY (padded to -84.05). This box necessarily overlaps the committed Dayton discovery box's southern edge (Dayton's min_lat is 39.35); overlap in a DISCOVERY bounding box is expected and harmless -- ownership is decided per-identity by the boundary reconciliation manifest and MARKET_ID_FIELD, never by which box a coordinate falls in.

coordinate_precision_disclosure: All lat/lng values in this file are low-precision (~2 decimal places, roughly 1km) approximate municipal-center reference points from general public geographic knowledge, rounded deliberately to avoid a false impression of survey-grade precision. They are seed points for bounded-radius provider queries only. A future sprint should replace them with a cited source (e.g. US Census TIGER/Line places or municipal open-data GIS) before any precision-dependent use.

scope_disclosure: 19 cells covering the tri-state OH-KY-IN Cincinnati regional metro per PTF-CINCINNATI-MARKET-FACTORY-001's mid-run boundary correction. The middletown-monroe cell is explicitly flagged for Cincinnati-Dayton boundary reconciliation before any identity found there is admitted to Cincinnati authority; see cincinnati-dayton-boundary-review.json. Kentucky and Indiana municipalities are IN-SCOPE Cincinnati identities under this corrected boundary, not spillover -- a genuine spillover manifest is reserved for identities found outside all nineteen cells (e.g. a hotel discovered in a KY/IN county not in the five/seven/three-county list).
